title: Working Capital Improvement
summary: Releasing cash by improving receivables, payables, inventory, and cash conversion cycle discipline.
definition: Releasing cash by improving receivables, payables, inventory, and cash conversion cycle discipline.
whyItMatters: PE cares because the initiative can convert operating diagnosis into measurable EBITDA, cash flow, growth quality, management accountability, or exit multiple support.
commonProblems: Management has anecdotes but no clean baseline.
The company tracks activity but not value impact.
Owners are unclear and initiatives compete for attention.
diagnosticQuestions: Where is the value leakage visible in the P&L, balance sheet, or operating dashboard?
Which segments, sites, customers, SKUs, vendors, or teams drive the variance?
What can be changed in the first 30, 60, and 100 days without breaking the business?
process: Define the value hypothesis and KPI baseline.
Segment the business to isolate where the opportunity lives.
Prioritize quick wins, structural fixes, and longer-term capability builds.
Assign owners, cadence, and benefits tracking.
Report progress through the value creation dashboard.
ebitdaLogic: The lever improves enterprise value by increasing EBITDA, releasing cash, making growth more durable, or creating a better diligence story that buyers can underwrite.
caseExample: In a sponsor-backed company, the team builds a baseline, targets the highest-variance segments, launches a 100-day sprint, and uses weekly value tracking to separate real savings or growth from one-time noise.
hundredDayPlan: Days 1-30: baseline data, confirm opportunity, name executive owner.
Days 31-60: launch pilots, install dashboard, remove blockers.
Days 61-100: scale what works, lock cadence, quantify run-rate impact.
commonMistakes: Treating the playbook as a one-time project instead of a management system.
Counting theoretical benefits that never hit EBITDA or cash.
Skipping change management with the operating team.

articleSections.title: Working Capital: The Hidden Source of Liquidity
body: In the capital-intensive world of private equity, working capital optimization is a critical lever for releasing 'trapped' liquidity that can be redeployed to pay down debt or fund strategic acquisitions. We view the balance sheet not as a static report, but as a dynamic engine where every dollar of inventory or accounts receivable (AR) represents a cost of capital. By tightening the 'Cash Conversion Cycle' (CCC), we can effectively generate 'free' cash flow without needing to grow the top line or cut essential operational costs.

Successful operating partners begin by establishing a baseline for Net Working Capital (NWC) as a percentage of revenue, benchmarking this against industry peers to identify structural inefficiencies. We utilize specialized 'Cash Management' tools like HighRadius or Kyriba to gain real-time visibility into the various components of NWC—inventory, receivables, and payables. This data-driven approach allows us to set granular targets for 'Day Sales Outstanding' (DSO), 'Days Inventory Outstanding' (DIO), and 'Days Payable Outstanding' (DPO) that are aligned with the fund's return targets.

The impact of a 10% reduction in NWC for a $500M revenue business is substantial. If the current NWC is 15% of sales ($75M), a 10% improvement releases $7.5M in cash directly to the balance sheet. Because this release occurs at a 1:1 ratio, it has a disproportionate impact on the investment's Internal Rate of Return (IRR), particularly in the early years of the hold period. We treat working capital optimization as a 'Day-1' priority to ensure that the portfolio company is self-funding its own transformation.
articleSections.callout: Cash is the lifeblood of the investment; every day it stays trapped in the balance sheet is a day it isn't creating value for the GP.

articleSections.title: Optimizing Receivables: The Art of DSO Reduction
body: Accounts Receivable (AR) is often the largest component of trapped cash, particularly in industries with fragmented customer bases or poor collection processes. We focus on 'DSO Reduction' by professionalizing the 'Order-to-Cash' cycle, ensuring that invoices are accurate, sent promptly, and followed up on systematically. By implementing automated AR platforms like Billtrust or Tesorio, we can reduce the 'collection friction' that leads to unforced delays in payment.

Mathematically, for a company with $20M in monthly billings, reducing the DSO from 45 days to 38 days releases roughly $4.6M in cash. This is achieved by tightening credit terms, eliminating billing errors that lead to disputes, and incentivizing the sales team to prioritize 'Cash Collection' over just 'Order Entry.' We often link the sales leadership's quarterly bonuses to 'Aged AR' metrics using CRM data from Salesforce, ensuring that the team responsible for the customer relationship is also accountable for the payment.

We also look at 'Dispute Management' as a key driver of AR health. By using root-cause analysis to identify why customers are withholding payment—whether due to shipping errors, pricing discrepancies, or product defects—we can fix the underlying operational issues. This not only improves cash flow but also enhances customer satisfaction, as the 'invoice-to-pay' process becomes a seamless part of the service experience. A clean AR ledger is a hallmark of a well-run PE-backed business and is highly valued by future acquirers.

articleSections.title: Inventory Management: DIO and SKU Optimization
body: In manufacturing and distribution, inventory is often where the most significant working capital gains are found. We focus on 'Days Inventory Outstanding' (DIO) by implementing rigorous 'Sales and Operations Planning' (S&OP) processes that align procurement with actual market demand. Using advanced inventory planning tools like Anaplan or o9 Solutions, we can optimize 'Safety Stock' levels and identify slow-moving or obsolete (SLOB) inventory that should be liquidated to free up warehouse space and cash.

Consider the impact of a 'SKU Rationalization' program on inventory levels. If a company carries 10,000 SKUs but 80% of its margin comes from just 1,500 of them, the remaining 8,500 SKUs are likely a massive drain on working capital and warehouse labor. By pruning the bottom 20% of non-performing SKUs and consolidating volume into the 'Power SKUs,' we can often drive a 15-20% reduction in DIO while simultaneously improving order fulfillment rates and reducing logistics complexity.

We also utilize 'Just-in-Time' (JIT) and 'Vendor-Managed Inventory' (VMI) strategies where appropriate to shift the burden of carrying stock back to the supplier. By integrating our ERP (e.g., SAP, Oracle, or Microsoft Dynamics) with our key vendors' systems, we can ensure that materials arrive exactly when they are needed for production. This 'lean' approach to inventory management not only releases cash but also reduces the risk of 'Inventory Write-downs' that can negatively impact the company's earnings quality during an exit process.

articleSections.title: Managing Payables: Strategic DPO Extension
body: While AR and Inventory focus on collecting and moving assets faster, managing payables is about strategically extending the 'Days Payable Outstanding' (DPO) without damaging vendor relationships. We negotiate standardized payment terms across the entire vendor base, often moving from 'Net-30' to 'Net-45' or 'Net-60' as part of a broader procurement transformation. By utilizing Source-to-Pay tools like Coupa or SAP Ariba, we can ensure that we are paying vendors exactly when the contract dictates, and not a day earlier.

Mathematically, extending DPO by 15 days for a company with $120M in annual external spend releases $5M in cash. To maintain supplier goodwill during this transition, we often implement 'Supply Chain Finance' (SCF) or 'Dynamic Discounting' programs using platforms like Taulia or C2FO. These tools allow vendors to be paid early by a third-party financier at a small discount, providing them with liquidity while allowing the portfolio company to maintain its extended DPO targets.

Effective payables management also requires a centralized 'Procure-to-Pay' (P2P) function that eliminates 'maverick' payments and ensures that all invoices are matched to a valid Purchase Order (PO). This control prevents the 'cash leakage' that occurs when invoices are paid twice or when unearned rebates are not captured. By institutionalizing these controls, we ensure that the treasury team has a predictable and optimized 'Cash Outflow' schedule, which is essential for managing debt service and covenant compliance.

articleSections.title: Sustainability and the Exit Premium
body: The final goal of our working capital initiatives is to embed a 'Cash Culture' within the organization that is sustainable through all market cycles. This involves making 'Free Cash Flow' a primary KPI for every department head, not just the CFO. We ensure that NWC metrics are reported on a weekly basis and are a central part of the monthly board deck, supported by a 'Working Capital Dashboard' that tracks DIO, DSO, and DPO against the VCP targets.

Mathematically, the sustainability of working capital improvements drives a significant 'Multiple Premium' at exit. A buyer will pay more for a company that can demonstrate it is 'Cash Efficient' and can fund its own growth through disciplined NWC management. We document the working capital processes as core operational competencies, showing that the improvements are driven by systematic changes in ERP and CRM workflows rather than 'one-time' collection pushes.

In the final 12 months before an exit, we perform a 'Working Capital Tidy-up' to ensure the balance sheet is as clean as possible for the 'Net Debt' adjustment. Because NWC is typically adjusted 'dollar-for-dollar' at closing, every dollar of released cash goes directly to the sellers' proceeds. By presenting an optimized, high-velocity balance sheet, we prove to the next owner that the company is a well-oiled machine, ready for its next phase of growth with minimal capital injection required.
